Name: Bot Auto Hack
Description:
[h2]Bot Auto Hack[/h2]

Ever watched a boarding raid deliver a small army of hostile robots, selected every one of them, clicked Hack, and discovered that a synchronized cyberattack can also produce a synchronized pile of irreparable cores? Well, have I got a suspiciously patient recruitment protocol for you!

Bot Auto Hack queues eligible hostile robotic Beings and gives each one its own ordinary Stardeus Hack attempt, one per simulation tick. Current Core hashes the Hack start tick with the robot's persistent ID before its 50% roll. The mod leaves that formula alone and handles the queue, status, and optional Firewall-removal work.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]Individual Hack Dispatch[/h3]
- Automatically finds and queues eligible hostile robotic Beings
- Provides a manual Hack All Hostile Bots command while automation is off
- Redirects Core's multi-selection Hack click into the same individual queue
- Starts at most one accepted Core Hack per simulation tick
- Uses Core's native per-bot outcome hash without patching or tracking the roll
- Revalidates every target immediately before dispatch and skips anything no longer eligible
- Waits while the simulation is paused

[h3]Control and Status[/h3]
- Requires the existing Rogue AI Signal Intrusion research
- Starts with automatic hacking disabled and stores the setting with the save
- Shows the current number of living robotic Beings carrying Core's Hacked condition below the top-bar widget
- Keeps active hacks, pending targets, started and skipped attempts, and recent activity visible in the controls panel
- Saves pending target IDs and request sources
- Uses AUMF's stable native widget and panel controls, which retain Core's existing theme behavior

[h3]Firewall Chip Handling[/h3]
- Makes Hack unavailable for bots protected by a working Firewall Chip
- Provides a separate Firewall-removal toggle that starts disabled and operates only while main automation is on
- Orders removal only for living, active, hostile, incapacitated robots with a removable working chip in the Implant slot
- Skips welded slots, conflicting surgery orders, and targets without a suitable vanilla surgery facility
- Registers Stardeus's ordinary Remove operation; the mod never removes or damages the implant directly
- Leaves accepted operations visible and cancelable through the vanilla Surgeries interface

[h2]Safety and Core Ownership[/h2]

Bot Auto Hack considers only active, non-biological Being entities. Ships, colonies, biological Beings, dead or inactive targets, friendly robots, coreless bodies, bots already being hacked, and robots protected by a working Firewall Chip remain outside the queue. Ship and colony hacking paths are never inspected or patched.

Every dispatched target goes through Stardeus's normal single-target Hack action. Current Core owns the per-bot outcome hash, 50% comparison, Hacked-condition duration, Firewall protection, mind/core requirement, faction change, critical-to-irreparable failure damage, and all resulting death behavior. Bot Auto Hack no longer patches the Hacked condition or stores retry outcomes. Turning main automation off disables Firewall removal and cancels only pending automatic entries; explicit manual and multi-selection requests remain queued.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Stardeus 0.15.0[/b] (validated on [b]v0.15.0-rc313.3190[/b]), [b]Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0[/b], and the existing Rogue AI [b]Signal Intrusion[/b] research. Firewall removal additionally requires an appropriate vanilla surgery facility.

In rc313, Sandbox can display Signal Intrusion as unlocked while Core's Hack action still checks its separate unlock-effect flag. This is a Core issue and Bot Auto Hack does not bypass it.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You choose the automation. Core keeps eligibility, the hashed coin flip, and the consequences. Bot Auto Hack gives every hostile robot its own turn.

[b]One bot. One tick. One gloriously independent bad decision at a time.[/b]
